quote: 1. You get recessions, you have stock market declines. If you don't understand that's going to happen, then you're not ready, you won't do well in the markets.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 2. There is always something to worry about. Avoid weekend thinking and ignore the latest dire predictions of newsletter writers.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 3. This is a stock picker's market, and stock pickers are made, not born.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 4. A lot of great fortunes in the world have been made by owning a single wonderful business.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 5. There's nothing wrong with cash. It won't help you, but it won't hurt you either, and it lets you sleep well at night.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 6. Know what you own, and know why you own it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 7. Owning stocks is like having children – don't get involved with more than you can handle.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 8. Everybody knows that if you're a lousy shopper, you're not going to do as well in the mall as if you're a sharp shopper. Why should you be any different in the stock market?
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 9. You only need a few good stocks in a lifetime to make a lot of money.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 10. Just because a stock goes down doesn't mean it can't go down more.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 11. Gentlemen who prefer bonds don't know what they're missing.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 12. Corporations, like people, change their names for one of two reasons: either they've gotten married, or they've been involved in some sort of unsavory activity they're trying to cover up.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 13. Behind every stock is a company. Find out what it's doing.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 14. The first task of the bargain hunter is to narrow the field and separate the solid prospects from the ones that are counting on hopes, prayers, and miracles.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 15. People go to the library and they do incredible research on a microwave oven. And then they'll go out and spend $10,000 on a stock because they heard a tip on the bus.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 16. If you're prepared to invest in a company, then you ought to be able to explain why in simple language that a fifth grader could understand, and quickly enough so the fifth grader won't get bored.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 17. Just because you buy a stock and it goes up does not mean you are right. Just because you buy a stock and it goes down does not mean you are wrong.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 18. In the long run, it's not just how much money you make that will determine your future prosperity. It's how much of that money you put to work by saving it and investing it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 19. There is no shame in losing money on a stock. Everybody does it. What is shameful is to stay in a stock, or worse, to buy more of it, when the fundamentals are deteriorating.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 20. You can lose money in a very short time but it takes a long time to be really good at investing.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 21. Every once in a while, the market does something so stupid it takes your breath away.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 22. Selling your winners and holding your losers is like cutting the flowers and watering the weeds.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 23. You can't see the future through a rear-view mirror.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 24. It's easier to figure out what's going to happen to earnings and the fundamentals of a company over the next five years than it is to figure out what's going to happen to the stock over the next three months.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 25. The key organ is the stomach, not the brain.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 26. Big companies have small moves, small companies have big moves.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 27. The simpler it is, the better I like it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 28. If you like the store, chances are you'll love the stock.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 29. The tortoise beats the hare in the market too, and, all in all, it's much easier being a tortoise, once you've made your peace with the plodding pace.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 30. In stocks, as in romance, ease of relationship is often directly proportional to distance kept.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 31. The real key to making money in stocks is not to get scared out of them.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 32. Nobody can predict interest rates, the future direction of the economy, or the stock market. Dismiss all such forecasts and concentrate on what's actually happening to the companies in which you've invested.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 33. If you spend more than 13 minutes analyzing economic and market forecasts, you've wasted 10 minutes.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 34. Stop listening to professionals!
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 35. The stock market demands conviction as surely as it victimizes the unconvinced.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 36. Insiders might sell their shares for any number of reasons, but they buy them for only one: they think the price will rise.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 37. When you sell in desperation, you always sell cheap.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 38. Invest in what you know.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 39. You have to keep track of where the future growth is coming from and when it's likely to slow down.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 40. Never invest in any company before you've done the homework on the company's earnings prospects, financial condition, competitive position, plans for expansion, and so forth.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 41. Although it's easy to forget sometimes, a share is not a lottery ticket, it's part ownership of a business.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 42. Never invest in any idea you can't illustrate with a crayon.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 43. The best way to handle a situation in which you love the company but not the current price is to make a small commitment and then increase it in the next sell-off.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 44. My diaries are full of such missed opportunities, but the stock market is merciful—it always gives the nincompoop a second chance.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 45. In the long run, a portfolio of well-chosen stocks and/or equity mutual funds will always outperform a portfolio of bonds or a money-market account.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 46. Time is on your side when you own shares of superior companies.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 47. The extra courage and conviction that come from understanding the company can make the difference between losing your shirt in a bear market and cleaning up in a bull market.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 48. If you're an investor, you're concerned with what will happen to your assets. If you're a trader, you're concerned with what will happen to the next guy.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 49. The p/e ratio of any company that's fairly priced will equal its growth rate.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 50. There's no reason to think brains alone will help you play the stock market. If that were true, a lot of professors would be a lot richer than they are.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 51. Frequently, there is no correlation between the success of a company's operations and the success of its stock over a few months or even a few years, but eventually, there is a 100 percent correlation between the success of the company and the success of its stock.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 52. A stock market decline is as routine as a January blizzard in Colorado. If you're prepared, it can't hurt you.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 53. Everyone has the brainpower to follow the stock market. If you made it through fifth-grade math, you can do it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 54. The more right you are about any one stock, the more wrong you can be on all the others and still triumph as an investor.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 55. When management owns stock, then rewarding the shareholders becomes a first priority, whereas when management simply collects a paycheck, then increasing salaries becomes a first priority.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 56. Charts are great for predicting the past.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 57. What you want to see on a balance sheet is at least twice as much equity as debt, and the more equity and the less debt the better.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 58. You don't have to be a genius to make money on Wall Street. You just have to be more disciplined than the average investor.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 59. Absent a lot of surprises, stocks are relatively predictable over ten to twenty years. As to whether they're going to be higher or lower in two or three years, you might as well flip a coin to decide.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 60. Markets go down, sometimes they go down a lot. If you are not ready for this, you shouldn't own stocks.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 61. Earnings are the key to success in investing in stocks. No matter what happens to the market, the earnings will determine the results.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 62. If you need the money in 1 or 2 years, you shouldn't be buying stocks.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 63. You don't have to kiss all the girls. I've missed my share of tenbaggers and it hasn't kept me from beating the market.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 64. Go for a business that any idiot can run – because sooner or later, any idiot probably is going to run it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 65. During the course of a lifetime of investing, dozens of stocks that you own will fluctuate 25 percent, 50 percent, or even more from the price you paid.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 66. Volatility is a fact of life on Wall Street, and instead of trying to avoid it, investors would do better to accept it as part of the process and get used to the fact that it exists.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 67. Spend at least as much time researching a stock as you would choosing a refrigerator.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 68. I can't recall ever once having seen the name of a market timer on Forbes' list of the richest people in the world. If it were possible to predict corrections, you'd think somebody would have made billions by doing it.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 69. Never invest in a company without understanding its finances. The biggest losses in stocks come from companies with poor balance sheets.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 70. Investing without research is like playing stud poker and never looking at the cards.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 71. The best stock to buy may be the one you already own.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 72. If you can't find any companies that you think are attractive, put your money in the bank until you find some.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 73. If you can't convince yourself, 'When I'm down 25% on a stock, I'm going to buy more,' you shouldn't be in the stock market.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 74. If you don't study any companies, you have the same success buying stocks as you do in a poker game if you bet without looking at the cards.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 75. Avoid hot stocks in hot industries. Great companies in cold, non-growth industries are consistent big winners.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 76. Far more money has been lost by investors preparing for corrections, or trying to anticipate corrections, than has been lost in the corrections themselves.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 77. If you stay half-alert, you can pick the spectacular performers right from your place of business or out of the neighborhood shopping mall, and long before Wall Street discovers them.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 78. The amateur investor is capable of making money from stocks and of beating the experts.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 79. In this business if you're good, you're right six times out of ten. You're never going to be right nine times out of ten.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 80. People who succeed in the stock market also accept periodic losses, setbacks, and unexpected occurrences. Calamitous drops do not scare them out of the game.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 81. Win or lose, everybody gets what they want out of the market.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 82. Whatever method you use to pick stocks or stock mutual funds, your ultimate success or failure will depend on your ability to ignore the worry cycle.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 83. If you invest $1,000 in a stock, all you can lose is $1,000, but you stand to gain $10,000 or even $50,000 over time if you're patient.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 84. The best place to find a tenbagger is right in your own backyard.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 85. The person that turns over the most rocks wins the game.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 86. Buy a stock the way you would buy a house. Understand and like it such that you'd be content to own it in the absence of any market.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 87. If you can follow only one bit of data, follow the earnings.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 88. The worst thing you can do is invest in companies you know nothing about.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 89. When even the former bears are becoming bulls, it's time to get cautious.
speaker: Peter Lynch

quote: 90. The best stocks to own are fast growers growing 20 to 25 percent a year.
speaker: Peter Lynch
